key_visual_traits: bronze to olive-green flanks with dark vertical bars
red to reddish-brown eye
upper jaw extending to the middle of the eye (not past it)
spiny dorsal fin joined to soft dorsal with a shallow notch
robust, torpedo-shaped body with a slightly forked tail
notes: Baseline species for relative scale index.

key_visual_traits: green to olive back fading to a pale belly
dark horizontal stripe running along the midline from gill to tail
upper jaw extending well past the rear edge of the eye
deeply notched dorsal fin separating spiny and soft sections
stocky body with a broad, slightly forked caudal fin
notes: Distinguished from smallmouth by jaw length and lateral stripe.

key_visual_traits: long, slender, torpedo-shaped body
dark olive-green flanks marked with rows of light bean-shaped spots
broad, flat duckbill-like snout with a wide mouth full of sharp teeth
single soft dorsal fin set far back near the tail
forked caudal fin and fully scaled cheek with lower half of gill cover bare
notes: Apex freshwater predator with distinctive elongated body.

key_visual_traits: long, cylindrical, heavy-bodied build with a rounded tail
very long undulating dorsal fin running most of the back
bony gular plate under the lower jaw
mottled olive to brown coloration with darker reticulated patterning
prominent dark eye spot (ocellus) at the base of the tail in males
notes: Living fossil; only surviving member of its order.

key_visual_traits: deep, laterally compressed disc-shaped body
olive to blue-green back with yellow-orange belly and faint vertical bars
solid black ear flap (opercular tab) at the rear of the gill cover
dark blotch at the rear base of the soft dorsal fin
small mouth not extending past the front of the eye
notes: Most recognizable panfish; black ear flap is diagnostic.

key_visual_traits: deep, strongly compressed silvery body speckled with irregular dark blotches
seven or eight dorsal spines (more than white crappie)
large, symmetric dorsal and anal fins of roughly equal size
broad head with upturned mouth and large eyes
faintly forked tail fin with mottled dark markings
notes: Irregular speckling (not vertical bars) distinguishes from white crappie.

key_visual_traits: stocky, slightly compressed body with a brassy olive coloration
bright red eye
rows of small dark spots forming faint horizontal lines on the lower flanks
six anal fin spines (more than most sunfish)
large mouth reaching to the middle of the eye
notes: Often called 'redeye'; distinctive red iris.

key_visual_traits: deep, round, laterally compressed body
brilliant orange belly and iridescent blue-green back with orange speckling
wavy turquoise lines radiating across the cheek and gill cover
black ear flap tipped with a bright crimson or scarlet spot
small mouth with a short upper jaw
notes: Red spot on the ear flap is diagnostic versus bluegill.

key_visual_traits: elongated oval body with a golden-yellow background color
six to nine dark vertical bars (tiger stripes) along the flanks
two clearly separated dorsal fins, the first spiny and the second soft
bright orange to red pelvic and anal fins
slightly humped back and a blunt, rounded snout
notes: Member of the true perch family; separated dorsals are key.

key_visual_traits: slender, elongated body with a slate-gray to olive back and silvery-white belly
deeply forked tail fin
four pairs of long whisker-like barbels around the mouth
scattered small dark spots on the sides (especially in juveniles and younger adults)
smooth scaleless skin with a small adipose fin ahead of the tail
notes: Forked tail and spotted sides separate from bullheads.

key_visual_traits: stout, thick-bodied shape with a broad flattened head
dark brown to nearly black back with a yellowish belly
squared-off or only slightly notched tail (not forked)
four pairs of dark barbels around the mouth
smooth scaleless skin and a small adipose fin
notes: Black bullhead; unforked tail distinguishes from channel cat.

key_visual_traits: deep, thick-bodied shape covered in large brassy-gold scales
long single dorsal fin with a serrated leading spine
two pairs of fleshy barbels at the corners of the mouth
downturned, sucker-like protrusible mouth
reddish-orange tint in the tail and anal fins
notes: Large scales and four barbels are diagnostic.

key_visual_traits: elongated cylindrical body tapering evenly toward the tail
dusky olive to bronze back fading to a cream or white belly
thick, fleshy, downward-facing sucker mouth with papillose lips
small scales that become noticeably smaller toward the head
single short dorsal fin with no spines and a slightly forked tail
notes: Ventral sucker mouth is the key identifier.

key_visual_traits: smooth, flattened dark olive to black carapace with red margin markings on the scute edges
bright yellow stripes on the head and neck with red streaks on the limbs and tail
yellow plastron (often unmarked in eastern subspecies, with a dark central blotch in midland and western forms)
webbed feet with clawed toes suited for swimming
small rounded head with a slightly notched upper jaw
notes: Most widespread native turtle in North America.

key_visual_traits: oval, moderately domed olive-green carapace with yellow streaks and dark vertical bars on the scutes
distinctive broad red or orange stripe behind each eye running along the side of the head
yellow plastron marked with dark blotches in each scute
yellow and green striped neck, limbs, and tail
fully webbed hind feet with long foreclaws in adult males
notes: Red postorbital stripe is the diagnostic field mark.

key_visual_traits: massive rough brown to olive carapace with three low longitudinal keels, often coated in algae
greatly reduced cross-shaped plastron leaving the limbs and neck largely exposed
long, thick, heavily saw-toothed tail nearly as long as the shell
large pointed head with a strongly hooked upper beak and powerful jaws
stout muscular legs with heavy claws and tubercles on the neck and limbs
notes: Long serrated tail and reduced plastron are diagnostic.

key_visual_traits: high-domed brown to black carapace with bright yellow or orange radiating blotches on each scute
hinged plastron that closes tightly against the carapace to fully enclose the body
short stout limbs with four toes on the hind feet (unlike the three-toed box turtle)
red to orange eyes in males, brown in females, set in a variably patterned head
slightly hooked upper jaw and a short tail
notes: Hinged plastron allows complete shell closure.

key_visual_traits: flat, round, pancake-like leathery carapace without scutes, olive to tan with dark ocelli or spots
row of small conical spines along the leading edge of the carapace
long tubular snorkel-like snout with nostrils at the tip
fully webbed feet with three clawed toes on each foot
slender head and long neck with pale stripes bordered by dark lines
notes: Pliable shell and tubular snout distinguish from hard-shelled turtles.

key_visual_traits: tall slate blue-gray body with a long S-curved neck and long yellow dagger-like bill
white face with a bold black plume extending back from above the eye
rusty-chestnut thighs and shoulder patches with black streaks down the foreneck
long dark legs trailing well beyond the tail in flight
shaggy plumes on the lower neck and back during breeding season
notes: Largest North American heron; neck held in an S-curve at rest.

key_visual_traits: stocky big-headed body with a shaggy double-pointed crest
slate blue-gray upperparts with a white collar and white underparts
broad blue-gray breast band (males) with an additional rusty belly band in females
heavy, straight, dagger-like black bill
short legs with small feet and a short square tail
notes: Females more colorful than males; double-crested silhouette is diagnostic.

key_visual_traits: large streamlined body with a glossy black head and thick dagger-shaped black bill
black-and-white checkered back with white rows of spots on the upper wings
vertical white neck stripes forming a partial collar and a bold black-and-white necklace
deep red eye in breeding plumage
legs set far back on the body with fully webbed feet
notes: Checkered back and white necklace define breeding adults.

key_visual_traits: long narrow wings held in a shallow M-shape with dark brown upperparts and white underparts
white head crossed by a broad dark eyestripe running through a yellow eye
streaked brown necklace across the upper breast (often heavier in females)
heavily hooked black bill and long bare grayish legs
reversible outer toe and spiny foot pads adapted for grasping fish
notes: Only raptor with a reversible outer toe; specialized fish eater.

key_visual_traits: male with an iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and pale gray body
female mottled brown with a dark crown and eyestripe and a mottled orange-and-black bill
bright blue speculum bordered by white bars on the secondaries in both sexes
yellow bill in males, orange legs in both sexes
upturned curly black central tail feathers in males
notes: Ancestral form of most domestic ducks; blue speculum is diagnostic.

key_visual_traits: male with an iridescent green-and-purple crested head marked by bold white facial stripes
chestnut breast flecked with white spots and buff flanks with fine black-and-white barring
red eye and a red-and-white bill in breeding males
female gray-brown with a white teardrop eye-ring and a small head crest
long square tail and sharp claws on the feet adapted for perching in trees
notes: One of the few ducks that nests in tree cavities.

key_visual_traits: stocky medium-sized heron with rich brown upperparts streaked in buff and dark brown
heavily streaked white and brown underparts providing reed-like camouflage
bold black malar stripe running down the side of the neck
yellow eye and a long straight yellowish dagger-shaped bill
greenish-yellow legs and a habit of pointing the bill skyward when alarmed
notes: Cryptic coloration and sky-pointing posture aid concealment in reeds.
